quests.title: The First Reading
quests.synopsis: One survivor's first dosimeter read books an Amber band. Decide whether the shelter keeps a ledger at all — or closes the book before its first page.

stages.title: The Dial
stages.narrativePrompt: The dosimeter needle twitches past the hundred mark before collapsing back. Whatever took the reading, the number is real now — it needs a sheet to live on. Dr. Vel holds the red pencil and waits for you to say whether the bunker is the kind of place that writes this down.

choices.text: Open the ledger. Write it down.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The book is opened. The name goes in with the number, in pencil so the drift can be corrected. Dr. Vel does not thank you. She starts ruling the next page.

choices.text: Close the book. This shelter does not keep that kind of paperwork.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The pencil goes down. No sheet is started, and the number is allowed to live only in the geiger counter's memory. For a season, the other three registers stay dark. The silence is recorded all the same.

stages.title: Booked
stages.narrativePrompt: The first entry is in. The corridor is quieter than it was, which is not the same as being calmer.

stages.title: Silence
stages.narrativePrompt: No ledger is started. Whatever the dial said, the shelter has willed itself to misremember it. The other registers wait out the season.

quests.title: The Sick of Room Seven
quests.synopsis: A Red-band survivor is named. The room has two beds and one morphine routine. Choose who is named first, and what the named are told.

stages.title: The Bed Order
stages.narrativePrompt: Room seven has two beds and one tray. Sister Omah lays the bed order on the table and waits. She will not shuffle it so one person's comfort costs another's care. Someone has to be named first, and whoever is named has to be told a thing.

choices.text: Keep the bed honest. Name both, split the care.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Both names go on the chart. The tray is split, the schedule kept. Neither is told a comfortable lie, and neither is told they are forgotten. The room stays honest.

choices.text: Hide one name. Spare one of them the knowing.
choices.outcomeNarrative: One name stays off the chart. That one sleeps easier for a while, and wakes, one day, to a bed order that does not quite match the room. The pencil marks do not lie; they were just made to.

choices.text: Draw on the Voluntary Register for a high-dose rotation that buys care.
choices.outcomeNarrative: A volunteer signs the hour. The care is bought, and bought at a price the ledger will itemise later. The room has its tray; whoever signed for it has a larger number than they did at dawn.

stages.title: Both Names
stages.narrativePrompt: The chart is full and honest. The room runs on halves and schedules.

stages.title: The Quietest Bed
stages.narrativePrompt: One chart has two names; the room has three mouths. The omission is a kindness and a lie, kept together.

stages.title: The Hour That Paid
stages.narrativePrompt: The tray is full and the chart is clean. Someone out in the corridor is carrying the number that paid for it.

quests.title: The Child's Number
quests.synopsis: A Cohort child is born. The parents ask the shelter to book a baseline. The numbers are a guess. Choose what to write.

stages.title: The Board
stages.narrativePrompt: The children's corridor has a chalkboard and a newborn. The midwife holds the chalk in pencil so it can be rewritten. The parents want a number written for their child — a baseline, a starting line. It is a guess no matter what you choose. Saria will not book a guess as a truth.

choices.text: Book low. Protect the child's story; risk a shock later.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The kinder number goes up in pencil. The child grows up believing the world owed them a gentler start. The dial will keep its own count, and the two may disagree, one quiet day.

choices.text: Book honest. A grim but maybe-true number.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The truer number as it stands is written down. It is corrected later, when the dial is willing to speak. No comfort was bought with it.

choices.text: Refuse to book. Let the child grow up uncounted.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The board stays blank. No guess at all. The child is not given a number, and so is not given a cage of one — but is also not given the small mercy of a true one. The refusal, for this child, is final.

stages.title: A Kinder Story
stages.narrativePrompt: The board shows a small hopeful number in pencil. It can be erased. The cost of erasing it later is the point.

stages.title: The Truer Number
stages.narrativePrompt: The board shows a grimmer figure in pencil. It stands there, subject to correction, and asks nothing of anyone.

stages.title: Uncounted
stages.narrativePrompt: The board is blank and stays blank. The child grows into a person without a baseline. Only the midwife's chalk remembers there was a choice.

quests.title: The Signed Hour
quests.synopsis: A volunteer has signed for high-dose work. They want to do it now, or wait. Sending them now books a worse dose; waiting risks the window closing.

stages.title: The Window
stages.narrativePrompt: The signature is signed. The task is the vented reactor corridor, and the volunteer is ready now, in this weather, with the dial reading what it reads. Send them now and the number is theirs to keep. Wait and the window may close before the task is possible at all. Either way, their reason is written down.

choices.text: Send them now. Book the worse dose.
choices.outcomeNarrative: They go now. The corridor takes its toll in numbers, and the reason they signed — whatever it was — is recorded beside the entry, unedited. The window does not wait, and neither, it turns out, did they.

choices.text: Wait. Risk the window closing.
choices.outcomeNarrative: They wait. The weather turns and the window narrows, but no worse number is banked today. The signature holds; the task may yet be done, or may quietly stop being possible. The reason is still on the page.

stages.title: Booked and Gone
stages.narrativePrompt: The entry is closed with its dose incurred. The reason stays written, whatever the price.

stages.title: A Waiting Signature
stages.narrativePrompt: The entry stays open, its dose not yet incurred. The reason is on the page, and the window is a matter of weather now.

quests.title: The Falsified Reading
quests.synopsis: A discrepancy is discovered between a scavenger's booked ledger band and recent field survey telemetry. Decide whether to correct the ledger or protect the worker.

stages.title: The Inked Discrepancy
stages.narrativePrompt: Dr. Vel lays two sheets beside each other in Room Six. The field survey recorded 340 mSv across the canal crossing, but the ledger line has been overwritten in faded graphite as 85 mSv. A worker with that low a reading keeps their surface clearance; the true reading would place them on the sick list. Dr. Vel watches you with her red pencil.

choices.text: Restore the true figure in red pencil. Truth over compassion.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Dr. Vel strikes through the graphite and writes 340 in red. The worker is pulled from surface expeditions immediately. The book is preserved, but the corridor is bitter.

choices.text: Leave the pencil figure. Let the worker keep their clearance.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The false line remains. The worker retains their clearance and returns to the surface, carrying biological radiation that the book pretends not to see.

stages.title: The Red Line
stages.narrativePrompt: The ledger is accurate. The worker sits on the bench outside Room Six, staring at their hands.

stages.title: Pencil Mercy
stages.narrativePrompt: The record holds a lie. The dial remembers, but the paper keeps the peace for now.

quests.title: The Stolen Dosimeter
quests.synopsis: A calibrated quartz dosimeter vanishes from the tool rack before a critical boiler overhaul. Find where it went.

stages.title: Empty Peg
stages.narrativePrompt: Piet Abar's bench has a gap in the felt tray. Dosimeter Tag 14 was taken during the night shift. Without it, whoever repairs the steam pipe in the sub-basement will work unmeasured — or someone took it to mask their own escalating burden.

choices.text: Confront the boiler technician and demand the return of the meter.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The technician gives up the meter from inside their boot. The reading inside is already 280 mSv. They stole it so they wouldn't be benched before earning their family's ration share.

choices.text: Issue an uncalibrated surplus meter and ignore the theft.
choices.outcomeNarrative: An old surplus meter with unknown drift is handed out. The repair proceeds, but whatever number it records will be a guess wrapped in brass.

stages.title: Recovered Meter
stages.narrativePrompt: The calibrated instrument is back on Piet's bench, its high reading logged in the ledger.

stages.title: Drifting Count
stages.narrativePrompt: Work goes on with uncalibrated tools. The ledger receives numbers that Piet will not certify.

quests.title: Child Over the Limit
quests.synopsis: An adolescent worker crosses into the Amber band. Saria Voss and Dr. Vel dispute whether they must be barred from workshop shifts.

stages.title: The Chalk Line
stages.narrativePrompt: Saria Voss stands in the doorway of the register hall, blocking Dr. Vel's ledger. The fourteen-year-old apprentice at the lathe clocked 115 mSv on their badge. By shelter rules, that books an Amber band and bars them from machine shop shifts. Saria argues the child's body is still growing and the number will panic the family; Dr. Vel insists the rule exists precisely because they are growing.

choices.text: Enforce the Amber restriction. Reassign the child to safe library duties.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The child is taken off the machine roster and assigned to cataloging paper in the archive. The lathe loses a pair of hands, but the child's exposure stops climbing.

choices.text: Issue a workshop apprentice waiver. The shelter needs machined parts.
choices.outcomeNarrative: A waiver slip is tucked into the badge case. Saria leaves the room without speaking. The lathe keeps running, and the apprentice's tag accumulates another week of workshop dust.

stages.title: Archive Quiet
stages.narrativePrompt: The child works quietly among the manuals. Their badge remains resting on the Green peg.

stages.title: The Machined Price
stages.narrativePrompt: Parts are produced on schedule. The apprentice's badge is shielded on paper, exposed in life.

quests.title: The Register Audit
quests.synopsis: Piet Abar detects a 15% calibration drift across last month's survey meters. Decide how to resolve the compromised records.

stages.title: The Drifted Month
stages.narrativePrompt: Piet sits with three disassembled survey meters on his felt mat. A hairspring fatigue in the master reference bench means every reading taken between Day 100 and Day 130 read 15% lower than reality. Dozens of survivors classified as Green or low Amber are physically deeper in burden than the book states.

choices.text: Recalibrate every meter and recalculate all affected entries.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Piet applies the calibration key and Dr. Vel works through the night adjusting twenty pages. Several workers discover they are in Amber or Red. The truth is restored, but morale takes a heavy blow.

choices.text: Fix the meters going forward; do not retroactively alter the past records.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The meters are reset, but the past pages stay unedited. Piet files the drift report in his private drawer. The past is allowed to remain artificially gentle.

stages.title: Corrected Ledger
stages.narrativePrompt: Every line in the ledger now matches calibrated truth. The shelter faces its reality with open eyes.

stages.title: Quiet Standard
stages.narrativePrompt: Future readings will be honest; past readings remain comfortable fictions.

quests.title: Black-Market Clean Bill
quests.synopsis: Forged Green-band clearance chits circulate in the corridors. Intercept the network or let the trade continue.

stages.title: The Stamped Slips
stages.narrativePrompt: A scavenger is caught at the Screening Station with a counterfeit clearance chit bearing a crude stencil of Dr. Vel's stamp. For five ration tins, a rogue clerk has been selling Green-band passes to workers desperate to avoid quarantine or sick-list restrictions.

choices.text: Shut down the ring, seize the stencils, and audit the screening checkpoint.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The stencils are destroyed and the rogue clerk is reassigned to waste duty. Entry screening at the station is reinforced with dual-signature verification.

choices.text: Confiscate the forged chits for institutional intelligence without public arrests.
choices.outcomeNarrative: You pocket the forged chits. The black market retreats underground, and you hold papers that can open doors without Dr. Vel's knowledge.

stages.title: Secure Checkpoint
stages.narrativePrompt: The screening station turnstiles click with verified stamps. Forgery is stamped out.

stages.title: Paper Levers
stages.narrativePrompt: You hold the forged slips. The ledger remains clean on the surface, compromised in the margins.

quests.title: The Broken Calibration Chain
quests.synopsis: The sealed reference source crystal used to calibrate shelter dosimeters has developed a micro-fracture. Repair it or guess.

stages.title: Fissure in the Standard
stages.narrativePrompt: Piet Abar holds up the lead container with trembling tongs. The cesium reference source inside has fractured, leaking particulate into its casing and making its baseline emission rate unstable. Without a calibrated standard, no dosimeter in the shelter can be accurately tuned.

choices.text: Allocate lead shielding and precision tools to build a new standard chamber.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Piet solders a new sealed chamber. The calibration chain is restored, and dosimeter tuning returns to laboratory precision.

choices.text: Rely on historical mathematical drift curves rather than spending scarce lead.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Piet sets aside his tools with a sigh. Future readings will be calculated from decay tables and estimates. The dials will speak, but only in approximations.

stages.title: True Calibration
stages.narrativePrompt: The new bench standard hums within its lead jacket. Every measurement in the shelter has an anchor again.

stages.title: Calculated Guesses
stages.narrativePrompt: The math replaces the crystal. The error bars grow wider with every passing week.

quests.title: Exposure for Essential Worker
quests.synopsis: The shelter's lead power engineer crosses into the Red band hours before a critical generator breakdown. Choose whether to order them back into the bay.

stages.title: The Generator & The Red Band
stages.narrativePrompt: The primary diesel turbine is throwing sparks, threatening a complete blackout of hydroponics and air filtration. The only survivor with the engineering skill to rebuild the governor valve is already at 320 mSv in the Dose Ledger. Entering the turbine pit now will push them toward Black band and irreversible sickness.

choices.text: Authorize an emergency override. The grid must stay online.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The engineer enters the turbine pit with a chelation kit and tools. The generator is saved and the power hum returns, but the engineer's badge reads 450 mSv upon return. Sister Omah begins preparing a bed in Room Seven.

choices.text: Refuse the override. Protect the engineer and institute rolling power cuts.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The engineer remains on the sick list. The turbine is throttled down, plunging half the shelter into darkness, but a life is not spent for electricity.

stages.title: Power Bought in Rem
stages.narrativePrompt: The lights stay bright. In Room Seven, the cost of that brightness lies under a wool blanket.

stages.title: Dark Corridor
stages.narrativePrompt: The corridors are dim, but the engineer lives to teach an apprentice when the crisis passes.

quests.title: The Missing Page
quests.synopsis: A page detailing early post-Exchange fallout exposures for founding families has been torn from the master ledger.

stages.title: Torn Binding
stages.narrativePrompt: Dr. Vel discovers that Sheet 04 — recording the first forty-eight hours of fallout penetration into Bunker Bay A — was cleanly sliced from the cloth binding with a surgical scalpel. Those records show which founding families received lethal doses before ventilation was sealed.

choices.text: Search the senior quarters, recover the sheet, and sew it back into the master ledger.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The sheet is found hidden beneath a floorplate in the council chamber. Dr. Vel threads waxed linen through the spine and binds it back in place. The founding families' sacrifice and secrets are permanently preserved.

choices.text: Allow the missing page to remain lost. The past cannot be healed by ink.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The torn stub remains in the book. Dr. Vel draws a single red line across the gap. The founders' history becomes an unprovable rumor, and the living move on.

stages.title: Complete Record
stages.narrativePrompt: Every page is intact. The ledger tells the whole story from Day One, unedited and unspared.

stages.title: The Red Stub
stages.narrativePrompt: A single red mark marks the gap in history. What happened in Bay A stays between the concrete and the dead.
